# Ruby Gillis

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c28 P13](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0013), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Role:** Teacher  <sub>[v1 c37 P34](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0034), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060)</sub>

## Appearance

Ruby was a handsome, showy girl with large, bright-blue eyes, a brilliant complexion, and a plump figure. She had long, beautiful golden-yellow hair worn in braids, though she later wore it styled up in town. Before her death from consumption, she grew very thin, with pale, transparent hands, overly bright eyes, and hectically brilliant cheeks.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P3](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0003), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005)_

## Personality

Ruby was a cheerful, merry, and good-tempered young woman who enjoyed the pleasant things in life. She was heavily preoccupied with young men and romantic attention, boasting frequently about her suitors. She was inclined to be sentimental and hysterical in frightening or emotional situations, such as when Anne fell off the roof or when Mr. Phillips gave his farewell speech. Towards the end of her life, she fought desperately to cling to life and feared death deeply, though she eventually passed away peacefully with a smile.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P39](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0039), [v1 c21 P2](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0002), [v1 c23 P16](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0016), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)_

## History

Ruby grew up in Avonlea as part of the circle of girls attending Avonlea School. During her school years, she joined Anne Shirley's story club, participated in school concerts, and joined the Queen's Academy preparation class taught by Miss Stacy. After graduating from Queen's, she secured a teaching position at Carmody, where she was widely pursued by local admirers. Following an attack of lung congestion during the winter, she developed galloping consumption and had to give up teaching. Throughout her illness she maintained a defiant pretense of health, continuing to talk gaily of her admirers and social plans. Shortly before her death, she opened up to Anne Shirley about her intense fear of dying and her unfulfilled wish to marry and have a family. She passed away quietly in her sleep the next night and was laid to rest in the Avonlea graveyard.

_Sources: [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c26 P20](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0020), [v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v1 c37 P34](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0034), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c14 P2](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0002), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)_

## Quotes

> I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It’s fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead—I just couldn’t. I’d die really of fright.  <sub>[v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001)</sub>

> Me! Why, I’m perfectly well. I never felt better in my life. Of course, that congestion last winter pulled me down a little. But just see my color. I don’t look much like an invalid, I’m sure.  <sub>[v3 c11 P57](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0057)</sub>

> Anne, it won’t be long now before I’ll be lying over there. You and Diana and all the rest will be going about, full of life—and I’ll be there—in the old graveyard—dead!  <sub>[v3 c14 P7](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0007)</sub>

> I don’t want to die. I’m afraid to die.  <sub>[v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011)</sub>

> I want to live. I want to live like other girls. I—I want to be married, Anne—and—and—have little children. You know I always loved babies, Anne. I couldn’t say this to any one but you. I know you understand. And then poor Herb—he—he loves me and I love him, Anne. The others meant nothing to me, but he does—and if I could live I would be his wife and be so happy. Oh, Anne, it’s hard.  <sub>[v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>
